transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brings me in is... I mean, I hardly eat right anymore. Some days it's just coffee and maybe a piece of bread, and my pants are hanging loose on me. I actually had to punch a new hole in my belt yesterday. It's this old leather belt my grandfather gave me—he used to work at the tannery down by the river before it closed up in the 90s. Used to smell like chemicals all the time, but he always had the best stories about the guys he worked with. Anyway, yeah, just coffee and bread mostly.
When you're eating less, is it because food doesn't interest you or you just don't feel hungry, or are you actively trying to avoid eating or control your weight?

Well, like I was saying, it's mostly just the coffee and the bread. It ain't because I'm trying to be skinny or go on some kind of diet, if that's what you mean. I just... I look at food and I don't care. I ain't got no appetite at all. 

It's weird because I used to love eating. Specially barbecue. There used to be this place off Highway 9, they had the best ribs. Cooked 'em slow over hickory wood. The guy who ran it, big guy named Earl, he always wore these funny aprons. One had a cartoon pig on it, I think. He closed up shop a few years back, moved to Florida or something. A lot of folks from around here move to Florida when they get older, you know? The humidity down there though, I don't know how they stand it. I went to Orlando once when I was a kid and I felt like I was breathing soup the whole time. 

But yeah, I just don't feel hungry anymore. That's why I'm barely eating and my clothes are all bagging off me.
Besides the changes in your eating, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I... I guess so. Most days I wake up and there's just this heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest. Like... like nothing good is waiting for me out there, you know? So I just want to keep my head down and stay in bed. 

My bed's actually not that comfortable anyway. It's this old mattress I got from a buddy of mine when he was moving out of his apartment over on Elm Street. Elm Street used to be real nice, lots of big trees, but then they had that storm a couple years back—knocked down half the power lines in the county. We were out of power for three days. Had to eat all the ice cream in the freezer before it melted. It was that Neapolitan kind. I always eat the strawberry first, then the vanilla, and leave the chocolate for last. I don't know why, just always done it that way since I was a kid. My mom used to buy it in those big plastic tubs. 

But yeah, I just feel down all the time. Like there ain't no point to getting up.
How long have you been feeling this way—the low mood, low energy, and not wanting to eat? Has it been going on for a couple of weeks, or longer?

Well, it ain't just a couple weeks. I'd say... this depressed spell has been hanging over me for about five months now. 

I know because it started right around the time my neighbor's dog had puppies. She's got this pitbull mix, real sweet dog named Roxy. Had a litter of six. Three of 'em were mostly white with these little brown spots over their eyes. I almost took one, but, well, like I said, I can barely feed myself right now, let alone a puppy. Plus, dog food is getting crazy expensive anyway. I was at the store—well, not the store, the gas station down the street—and a small bag of dog chow was almost double what it used to cost. Everything's going up like that. Gas, milk... my uncle used to deliver milk back when they did it in glass bottles. He said the glass made it taste colder. I don't know if that's true, but he swore by it. He had this old white delivery truck that rattled so loud you could hear him coming from three streets over. 

But yeah, it's been about five months of feeling this way.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory or your ability to concentrate and stay focused on tasks, like following a conversation or remembering appointments?

Yeah, I guess so. It's... it's real hard to focus lately. Like, if I try to look at forms or, you know, my bills, my mind just kinda slips off 'em. I can't keep my attention on it at all. And it's even bad when I'm just trying to do regular stuff. Like I'll go to the store and just stand there in the aisle, completely stuck trying to figure out which can of soup to buy. 

It's usually the chicken noodle. I used to always get the kind with the stars in it. You know, the little pasta stars? My grandma used to make that for me when I was sick. She had this old pot, it was bright orange enamel, chipped on the bottom. She'd boil the soup and serve it with these saltine crackers that she kept in a tin box with a picture of a windmill on it. I think the tin was from some cookies she got for Christmas one year. She loved Christmas. She'd put up this fake silver tree and shine a little color wheel light on it so the branches would turn red and blue and green. It was real pretty, even if it was just plastic. 

But yeah, I just... I can't concentrate on nothing. Just stand there staring at the soup cans like an idiot.

Have you had any recent medical problems, head injuries, or new neurological symptoms—like headaches, dizziness, weakness, or changes in coordination—around the time these mood and concentration issues started?

No, no, nothing like that. No head injuries or... or new medical problems. I haven't been dizzy or anything. 

I did bump my head on the kitchen cabinet a few weeks ago, though. Left the door open when I was getting a glass. It was one of those heavy glass mugs, the kind they give you at that root beer place? A&W, I think it was. We used to go there after Little League games. My coach was this guy named Mr. Henderson, he drove a station wagon with wood panels on the sides. Real nice guy, but he always chewed on a toothpick. Like, he'd have it in his mouth the whole game, just rolling it around. I always wondered if he ever accidentally swallowed one. That seems dangerous, you know? Like it could poke a hole in your stomach or something. My aunt swallowed a fish bone once, had to go to the emergency room. They had to use these long tweezers to pull it out of her throat. She wouldn't eat fish for years after that. Not even fish sticks. 

But no, my head is fine. No headaches or nothing like that. Just the... the not being able to focus and feeling so down.
Have you had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself, or wished you wouldn't wake up?

No, I... I haven't been thinking about hurting myself or nothing like that. I don't wish I wouldn't wake up, even though sleeping is about the only thing I feel like doing lately. 

But no, no thoughts of dying. I did go to a funeral last month, though. My cousin's husband. He wasn't that old, either, maybe fifty? Heart attack. Just dropped right there in the driveway while he was washing his truck. It was a nice truck, too—one of those big Ford F-150s, bright red. He used to keep it so clean you could see your reflection in the hubcaps. He was always out there with a bucket and sponge on Saturday mornings. Used that blue soap, the kind that smells like bubblegum? I bought some of that soap once for my old Honda, but I never really got around to using it much. The bottle just sat in my garage until the plastic got all brittle and cracked. It leaked blue goo all over a box of old magazines I had out there. Mostly old Sports Illustrateds. I used to love reading about baseball. 

But no, I'm not thinking about hurting myself or dying. Just... just feeling real low.
